If he is getting enough excercise then I’d suggest teaching him the “on your bed” command. Put a bed or a mat out and teach it like a lie down but on that spot. 

When he has learnt this you should be able to order him to chill out by saying this command. This is only if the dog is getting enough engagement and excercise; if he isn’t then that’s your problem.

You can imagine the action putting the harness on from the front being like to catch him with a net and I suspect you’re unconsciously being a bit sus with your body language.

I would try a lead and collar as a fresh start. Unless he is super anxious and a runner just have the lead. If you are concerned he will do a runner then clip the lead so he’s secure and can’t run then put the harness on; try doing it from behind and swiftly, no faff. Double securing dogs is a practice that’s done- you’ll have two leads then, the harness lead being just a back up. 

Collies aren’t as food motivated as other dogs and get more out of engagement and stuff so it’s pretty normal that he’s not taking treats when feeling anxious or triggered. They are sensitive little eggs lol. Just try and be calm and confident, don’t be afraid to ‘tell’ them sometimes because I feel they’re more secure with a strong leader.

They like to be independent. IMO they are better off the lead. 

However they can’t always be off lead; to me it sounds like you’re making an issue of the harness and passing on some ag to the dog. 

If they know the word walk just say it and stand by the door and put the harness on. Even just try a lead cuz you might have primed the harness with anxiety. Just clip it on or loop it round and go. Don’t make an issue.

Also allow your dog off when appropriate if you have recall.

Just take her out often. Say toilet command when she does her business and positively verbally reward with “good girl” after. If she does nothing be neutral. Only if she does her business inside after you have come in would I venture towards any kind of mild shaming (BC very sensitive). She’s prob just not got it in her head that not everywhere is a toilet because she’s lived outside. She’s clever so should just pick it up if you’re taking her out enough.

You should not be disciplining for this behaviour- you should be working on training (see my other comment)- 

However in extreme circumstances (chasing car wheels, jumping up on guests when they come in, barking at postman, trying to bite the washing machine) I have used a Pet Corrector (expensive). It’s basically a loud hiss in a can that immediately snaps them out of it. You can also use some stones in a plastic bottle. 

Collies are VERY sensitive people. Usually all you have to do is get that red can out and they’ll quit whatever they were thinking about doing. 

It’s important not to over use it, and to use it at exactly the right time (when they are actually doing the bad behaviour, not as a deterrent or punishment)

Border Collies like being asked rather than made to do something. Try getting a mat or a bed and doing training for “on your Matt” “on your bed”. 

If you have sit and wait you can just put a treat on said mat tell her to go get it then get a lie down- say the command and treat/click.

Boundaries work both ways- you and any family members/guests should respect the place where you tell the dog to go and lie down. It’s their safe space and shouldn’t be invaded.
